It is the only {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=shikinaisha small shrine}} in Sanda City, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}} of former {{ill|Kawabe District, Hyōgo|ceb|Kawanabe-gun|es|Distrito de Kawabe|fr|District de Kawabe|id|Distrik Kawabe, Hyōgo|it|Distretto di Kawabe|ja|川辺郡|ko|가와베군|pl|Powiat Kawabe|ru|Кавабе (уезд, Хёго)|zh|川邊郡|qid=Q1042053}}. {{nihongo|'''Takamefu Shrine'''|高売布神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}. It is located in {{ill|Settsu Province|ca|Província de Settsu|cs|Provincie Seccu|de|Provinz Settsu|eo|Provinco Seccu|es|Provincia de Settsu|fa|ولایت ستسو|fr|Province de Settsu|gl|Provincia de Settsu|hak|Settsu-koet|id|Provinsi Settsu|it|Settsu (provincia)|ja|摂津国|ko|셋쓰국|lt|Seccu žemė|nl|Settsu (provincie)|pt|Província de Settsu|ru|Сэтцу (провинция)|simple|Settsu Province|sk|Seccu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Сецу|tr|Settsu (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сеццу|zh|攝津國|zh_min_nan|Settu-kok|zh_yue|攝津國|qid=Q864163|lt=Settsu Province}}.
The honden and wooden {{ill|Komainu|ar|كوماينو|as|কোমাইনু|de|Komainu|et|Komainu|fa|کومااینو|fr|Komainu|hu|Komainu|ja|狛犬|ko|코마이누|pl|Komainu|pt|Komainu|ru|Комаину|simple|Komainu|sq|Komainu|zh|狛犬|qid=Q20155846}} are designated national {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|de|Wichtiges Kulturgut Japans|es|Bien Cultural Importante de Japón|fi|Japanin tärkeä kulttuuriomaisuus|fr|Bien culturel important|id|Properti Kebudayaan Penting (Jepang)|it|Bene culturale importante (Giappone)|ja|重要文化財|ko|일본의 중요문화재|ro|Patrimoniu cultural important al Japoniei|simple|Important Cultural Properties of Japan|th|ทรัพย์สินทางวัฒนธรรมที่สำคัญ (ญี่ปุ่น)|tr|Önemli Kültürel Varlık (Japonya)|uk|Важливі культурні пам'ятки Японії|zh|重要文化財|qid=Q1188622}}.

== Enshrined deities ==
The main deity is {{ill|Shitateruhime|fr|Shitateruhime|ja|シタテルヒメ|simple|Shitateru-hime|zh|下照姬|qid=Q11307233|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto}} (Takahime-no-Kami), with {{ill|Ame no Wakahiko|az|Ame-no-Vakahiko|fr|Ame no Wakahiko|it|Ame no Wakahiko|ja|アメノワカヒコ|ko|아메노와카히코|pl|Młodzian Potrafiący się Oderwać od Nieba|zh|天稚彥|qid=Q10940674|lt=Ame-no-Wakahiko-no-Mikoto}} as associated deity.

== History ==
It is traditionally said to have been founded in the time of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ar|الإمبراطورة سويكو|ast|Emperatriz Suiko|azb|امپراتریس سویکو|bcl|Emperatris Suiko|be|Імператрыца Суйка|ca|Suiko|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سویکۆ|cs|Suiko|de|Suiko|es|Suiko Tennō|eu|Suiko|fa|امپراتریس سوئیکو|fi|Suiko|fr|Suiko|hak|Suiko Thiên-fòng|he|סויקו, קיסרית יפן|hu|Szuiko japán császárnő|id|Suiko|it|Suiko|ja|推古天皇|ka|სუიკო|ko|스이코 천황|la|Suiko (imperatrix)|nl|Suiko|pl|Suiko|pt|Suiko|ru|Императрица Суйко|sh|Carica Suiko|simple|Empress Suiko|sl|Cesarica Suiko|sv|Suiko|ta|பேரரசி சுய்கோ|th|จักรพรรดินีซูอิโกะ|tl|Emperatris Suiko|tr|Suiko (imparatoriçe)|uk|Імператор Суйко|uz|Imperator Suiko|vi|Thiên hoàng Suiko|zh|推古天皇|zh_classical|推古天皇|zh_min_nan|Suiko Thian-hông|zh_yue|推古天皇|qid=Q298057}}. There is also a theory relating it to the founding of {{ill|Mefu Shrine (Takarazuka)|fr|Mefu-jinja|ja|売布神社 (宝塚市)|qid=Q3304192|lt=Mefu Shrine}}, another shikinaisha in the same Kawabe District. In the Heian period, {{ill|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|ast|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|es|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|fa|میناموتو نو میتسوناکا|fr|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|it|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|ja|源満仲|ko|미나모토노 미쓰나카|oc|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|pt|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|sv|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|zh|源滿仲|qid=Q2531241}}, who held vast estates in the region, is said to have made it the district sōsha. There is a tradition that Mitsunaka planted a {{ill|Zelkova serrata|ar|زلكوفا منشارية|arz|زلكوفا منشاريه|az|Zelkova serrata|ceb|Zelkova serrata|cs|Zelkova pilovitá|da|Japansk zelkova|de|Japanische Zelkove|es|Zelkova serrata|eu|Japoniar zelkoba|fa|نارون ژاپنی|fi|Idänselkova|fr|Zelkova serrata|frr|Zelkova serrata|hu|Japán gyertyánszil|id|Terbas jepang|ja|ケヤキ|ko|느티나무|lt|Japoninis skirpstulas|nl|Japanse zelkova|no|Keaki|pl|Brzostownica japońska|pt|Zelkova serrata|pwn|tjeves|ru|Дзельква пильчатая|sco|Zelkova serrata|sv|Zelkova serrata|tr|Zelkova serrata|vi|Zelkova serrata|war|Zelkova serrata|zh|榉树|zh_yue|櫸樹|qid=Q920344}} tree.

At some period it was also called Kazuki Daimyōjin, Tsuki-no-miya, and Sai-no-miya. A shrine-name plaque reading “Senior First Rank Kazuki Daimyōjin,” donated from {{ill|Hōkyō-ji Temple|ja|宝鏡寺|qid=Q11452697}} in Kyoto, remains in the haiden.

== Rituals and annual events ==
*Senbon-tsuki: on October 7, fathers called "hatsutō" (whose children were born in the past year) sing "Sosoba-tsuki-uta" while making "chigiri-mikyo," rice cakes offered at the annual festival.
*Annual festival: on October 9, "chigiri-mikyo" is offered before the deity, and "hatsutō" carry the {{ill|Mikoshi|ar|ميكوشي|cs|Mikoši|de|Mikoshi|es|Mikoshi|fa|میکوشی|fr|Mikoshi|gd|Mikoshi|hr|Mikoshi|hy|Միկոշի|id|Mikoshi|it|Mikoshi|ja|神輿|ko|미코시|mk|Омикоши|ml|മികോഷി|pa|ਮਿਕੋਸ਼ੀ|pl|Mikoshi|pt|Mikoshi|ru|Микоси|simple|Mikoshi|tl|Omikoshi|tr|Mikoshi|uk|Мікосі|zh|神轎|qid=Q979940}}.
